patches.old: The CARS section gives you approximately 8-9 minutes per passage.
patches.new: The CARS section is 53 questions across 9 passage sets in 90 minutes — about 10 minutes per passage, reading and questions together.
patches.reason: AAMC lists 53 questions and 9 passage sets in 90 minutes, which is ~10 minutes per passage, not 8–9.

patches.old: A useful benchmark: most students should spend approximately 3-4 minutes reading a passage and 5-6 minutes on the questions.
patches.new: A useful benchmark within those 10 minutes: roughly 4 minutes reading the passage and 6 minutes on its 5–7 questions.
patches.reason: Makes the split add up to the real ~10-minute budget.

visual.title: Ten minutes per passage
visual.alt: A bar splits ten minutes into about four minutes of reading and six of questions. Six steps: a 15-second preview of the title and first and last sentences; read the first paragraph carefully to find and mark the thesis; read body paragraphs with a three-to-five-word note on what each does; read counterarguments critically, asking whether the author agrees; read the final paragraph for the refined thesis; and take a 15-second review to state the argument in one sentence. Two columns list what to annotate (thesis, paragraph function, tone words, transitions, a question mark where you lost the thread) and what not to (names, dates, statistics, examples, full sentences). A closing strip maps these habits to main idea, tone, function, inference and strengthen/weaken questions.
visual.caption: Timings are a guide, not a rule — the point is that reading work saves question time.
